access: A read-only connection to the PostgreSQL source, preferably a replica, with SELECT on the extracted tables; optionally pg_read_all_stats to see other sessions in pg_stat_activity

presentation.name: Extract from PostgreSQL incrementally without straining the production database
presentation.summary: Reads a PostgreSQL source in batches by (updated_at, id) that neither skip nor repeat rows, keeps each batch on an index, and keeps the job's transactions, timeouts and connections from hurting the application that owns the database.
benefits: Resumes from an (updated_at, id) keyset with an upper bound that late-committing transactions cannot slip behind
Reads EXPLAIN to confirm each batch uses an index and costs the same at the end of the table as at the start
Proposes only the index the extraction needs, with what it costs the source and how to build it without blocking writes
Finds the long or idle-in-transaction sessions that stall vacuum, and proposes statement and idle timeouts for the job's role
Counts the job's connections, including Spark JDBC partitions, against the source's max_connections
